bias_direction: Toward treating the criterion as more than it is, because this batch went looking for exactly one thing after being criticised for not going looking for it, and found it. Having framed it in advance as the highest-value target left, there was every incentive to write it up as the answer. It is not the answer: it is a regulator's assertion with no participants, no measurement and no citation, which is the same evidential class as the ceilings it explains — the only difference is that it says what the number is for. The specific overreach to watch is the claim that its mechanism stops the owner's 0-degree regress. That is my inference joining a sentence about sustained effort to a statement about monotonic curves; the source does not mention dose-response, and a reader could reasonably call it a tidy story rather than a finding.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: A reviewer should ask whether four Co-1 zeroes are being converted, a little too smoothly, from a failure into a result. The record presents the asymmetry — disabled people published on access, regulators published on numbers — as a fact about the evidence base. An alternative reading is that four searches, three of them a single query at a single organisation's website, is thin evidence for a claim about what an entire community has and has not published, and that the batches have been searching in the register the corpus already speaks: institutional documents in indexed places. Lived-experience knowledge about gradient plausibly exists in forums, in wheelchair-skills training material, in occupational-therapy practice and in the Co-2 professional-body literature the contract names first and no batch has yet run at all. On that reading the asymmetry finding is premature and the honest statement is narrower: four institutional Co-1 sources were checked and none carried a figure. The counter is that each zero was well-formed and individually diagnosed, and that naming a pattern is how the next batch knows where not to look again. But the reviewer is right that Co-2 — OT professional-body CPGs, co-primary under the tier system and untouched across three batches — is the gap this record should be naming instead of a pattern.
